Modelled Seroprevalence for Serosurvey Age Bands

Source: R/serosurvey.R
modelled_seroprevalence.Rd

Converts immunity by model age group from [run_immunity_history()] into the share expected to test seropositive in each age band of a serosurvey taken at the end of the run.

Usage

modelled_seroprevalence(
  history,
  age_min,
  age_max = NA,
  sensitivity = 1,
  specificity = 1,
  vaccine_seropositive = 1,
  maternal = FALSE
)

Arguments

history

Output of [run_immunity_history()] with `year_end` the survey year (for `maternal = TRUE` it needs `keep_params = TRUE`).

age_min, age_max

Lower and upper age of each band in years, with the upper limit inclusive as surveys report it (`5` and `9` for "5-9 years"); use `NA` for an open top band. Fractional ages are allowed (months / 12).

sensitivity, specificity

Assay sensitivity and specificity. Default 1.

vaccine_seropositive

Share of vaccine-protected people who test positive. Default 1.

maternal

Logical; count maternal antibody in infants as seropositive? Default `FALSE`.

Value

Numeric vector of expected seropositive shares, one per band.

Details

The true seropositive share in a model age group is $$p = \textrm{immune\_infection} + v \cdot \textrm{immune\_vaccine} + m \cdot \textrm{susceptible}$$ where `v` (`vaccine_seropositive`) is the share of vaccine-protected people who still have detectable antibody and `m` is maternal protection (only when `maternal = TRUE`), counted as antibody among those not otherwise immune. Model age groups are weighted by population and by how much of each group the band covers, taking ages to be spread evenly within a group. The test then gives $$p_{obs} = \textrm{sensitivity} \cdot p + (1 - \textrm{specificity}) (1 - p).$$

Examples

h <- list(by_age = data.frame(population = c(100, 100), immune_infection = c(0.1, 0.5),
                              immune_vaccine = c(0.6, 0.4), susceptible = c(0.3, 0.1)),
          age_breaks = "0;5;Inf")
modelled_seroprevalence(h, age_min = c(0, 2), age_max = c(4, 9))
#> [1] 0.700 0.825
